section_summary: This section begins with U.S. policy papers on Japanese assets in Siam and broader Far Eastern Commission proposals for occupation costs and Japanese external assets. Later records address news-service cable charges, wartime Japanese currency, and Joseph Dodge’s economic stabilization advice. Correspondence from Bangkok and Washington revisits enemy assets, claims, military aid, and communism in Thailand.

subfiles.title: Japanese Assets in Siam
subfiles.about: The division proposes agreeing on a departmental approach to Japanese assets in Siam before reopening talks with Siam.
subfiles.summary: Proposes an agreed internal course while discussion with Siam is deferred.

subfiles.title: Disposition of Japanese Assets in Siam
subfiles.about: The memorandum reviews custody, liquidation, and possible transfer of Japanese assets in Siam.
subfiles.summary: It recounts the joint British-American supervision of enemy assets, liquidation proceeds, and the unresolved question of Siamese and Allied war claims. It compares proposed U.S. and British positions on Japanese external assets and argues that Siam should gain sovereign control. It recommends seeking British agreement and comments from the ambassadors in London and Bangkok.

subfiles.title: Definition of Japanese Occupation Costs and the Priority to Be Accorded Their Repayment
subfiles.from: United States delegation; circulated by Nelson T. Johnson
subfiles.to: Far Eastern Commission, Committee No. 1: Reparations
subfiles.about: The proposal defines occupation costs and sets priorities for recovering them from Japanese assets.
subfiles.summary: The U.S. delegation proposes first priority for non-yen import advances, followed by civilian and military repatriation costs. It identifies Japanese exports, certain external assets, and liquid domestic assets as possible sources, with Siam excepted from the external-assets category.

subfiles.title: Disposition of Japanese External Assets
subfiles.doc_type: draft policy paper with discussion appendix
subfiles.to: SANACC and the U.S. member of the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: The draft sets out U.S. policy for Japanese assets outside Japan and explains its proposed exceptions.
subfiles.summary: The paper defines external assets and Japanese ownership, then generally proposes that countries holding such assets retain them. Special provisions cover neutral countries, Siamese war-damage claims, Germany, and protected property such as diplomatic, religious, charitable, and artistic assets. Its discussion weighs reparations policy, Soviet removals from Manchuria, and the political consequences of attempting to recover assets from other governments.

subfiles.title: Payment of Japanese Share of Cable Charges by News Services
subfiles.about: The memorandum recommends allowing news services to pay Japan’s share of cable charges in yen.
subfiles.summary: It reviews Army funding and news-company reactions, then recommends supporting SCAP’s proposal for full yen payment. The Japanese cable charges averaged about $3,500 monthly.

subfiles.title: Counterfeit Dollars, Presumably
subfiles.about: The embassy submits a photograph of a Japanese-issued hundred-dollar note found in Kabul and asks about its history.
subfiles.summary: Reports notes traced through traders to Rangoon and requests Treasury comment.

subfiles.title: Japanese Invasion Currency: Reply to Kabul
subfiles.about: The Department relays Treasury’s explanation of the photographed Japanese invasion currency.
subfiles.summary: Treasury says the wartime currency ceased circulating after the war.

subfiles.title: Draft Reply on Japanese Invasion Currency
subfiles.about: A draft gives Treasury’s assessment of the Japanese hundred-dollar occupation note.
subfiles.summary: States that Japanese occupation notes were mass-produced and no longer circulated.

subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement for Tokyo Despatch
subfiles.about: The form designates a replacement record copy for a missing Tokyo despatch original.
subfiles.summary: Designates a substitute record copy for filing.

subfiles.title: Transmitting Statement by Minister Joseph M. Dodge and Editorial Comment
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards Dodge’s economic statement and Japanese editorial reactions.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Dodge’s call for fiscal restraint and export growth.

subfiles.title: Japanese Editorial Comment on Minister Dodge’s Statement
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Translated Japanese editorials assess Dodge’s proposals on stabilization, budgets, credit, and the yen.
subfiles.summary: Editorials from several Japanese newspapers discuss balanced budgets, reduced subsidies and inflationary bond finance, production, exports, and uncertainty over yen devaluation.

subfiles.title: Personal Letter on Enemy Assets and Thailand Policy
subfiles.about: Stanton discusses Thai enemy assets, military aid, communism, and personal matters.
subfiles.summary: Stanton favors eventual transfer of enemy assets but urges caution because of their management and unsettled claims. He requests details of military aid and authority for stronger discussions with Thai officials about communism.

subfiles.title: Reply to Stanton on Enemy Assets and Thailand Policy
subfiles.about: Landon replies on enemy assets, claims, arms, regional communism policy, and the Point Four program.
subfiles.summary: Landon expects Thailand to receive the enemy assets and reports work toward settling the remaining Scholtz claim. He describes the military-aid announcement, proposed Commonwealth cooperation against communism, and efforts to settle policy on gold in Tokyo. He also says details of the Point Four program are not yet available.

subfiles.title: Routing Note on Treasury Action
subfiles.about: The note records transfer of action to Treasury and routes a copy for information.
subfiles.summary: Requests return of the yellow copy after OFD routing.

subfiles.title: Incoming Airgram Record Copy
subfiles.about: A largely illegible incoming-airgram cover bears filing and routing marks for currency correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Preserves the permanent-record-copy instructions and routing marks.

subfiles.title: Japanese Occupation Currency: Reply to The Hague
subfiles.about: The telegram assesses currency described by the embassy as probable Japanese military or occupation issue.
subfiles.summary: Says physical examination is needed, but the notes appear valuable only as souvenirs.

subfiles.title: Treasury Request to Transmit Currency Cable
subfiles.from: Treasury Department, Office of International Finance
subfiles.about: Treasury asks State to transmit its assessment of suspected Japanese occupation currency to The Hague.
subfiles.summary: Supplies cable text saying the described currency has souvenir value only.

subfiles.title: Inquiry About Exchanging Japanese and Chinese Currency
subfiles.about: Johnson asks whether three pieces of Japanese and Chinese paper currency can be exchanged for U.S. dollars.
subfiles.summary: Requests advice on the enclosed paper currency.

subfiles.title: Reply to Charlie Johnson on Foreign Paper Currency
subfiles.from: Gordon Strong, for the Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: State returns Johnson’s notes and explains why exchanging them for dollars would likely be fruitless.
subfiles.summary: The Department cannot handle exchanges and considers the notes’ present value too small to justify bank conversion.
